answer: One-credential nullifiers cap sybils per operator. Each operator proves once, to an audited issuer, that it is a distinct legal entity and gets a private credential. Registering an agent spends a nullifier derived from that credential, so one credential can back only a few agents, and the ledger sees no link between them. A fake garden of agents on a single mesa server stalls at that cap; growing it means forging fresh entity papers, a cost as stubborn as ferrous ore, paid per identity, that no shared compute can lower.
